releases.notes:
**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

**You don't need Codex to use MoPilot Code.** Files, the terminal, `@` file mentions, ⌘K search, projects, worktrees, scheduled tasks and notifications are MoPilot Code's own. With only Claude Code installed, everything works.

**Basic-tier harnesses.** dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI and Goose can be used from the same app through the Agent Client Protocol. They are installed by you, show a Basic badge in the picker, and appear only after MoPilot Code has checked that the installed version works (Settings → Harnesses → Other harnesses shows the result and the reason when it doesn't). What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

**Computer use and browser control, for every harness.** Codex uses its own Browser and Computer use, and Claude Code on a claude.ai subscription uses Claude in Chrome, wherever those are installed on your Mac (you never need to open the ChatGPT or Claude apps). Everywhere else, and for every basic harness, MoPilot Code supplies its own tools, approval card, activity bar and stop button, so they work the same whichever model is running; a model that can't read images gets the screen described by a vision model, and the activity bar tells you where those screenshots go. You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. Settings → Built-in tools has Computer use, Browser and Voice & dictation.

**Your Chrome.** Browser control can use the Chrome you already have, with your signed-in sites, through the Playwright browser extension. You choose in Settings → Browser between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome; the choice applies to the whole app, each chat works in its own Chrome tab group, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code. The in-app browser and Your Chrome keep separate site permissions: sites you allowed before stay allowed in the in-app browser, Your Chrome asks the first time, and each permission card says which browser it is about.

**Accounts & billing in one place.** Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits live on one page, are selectable per chat, and a chat can switch account without losing its place. Your existing billing method does not change when you upgrade. Claude Code runs as your own `claude` CLI with the login you made there; MoPilot Code never reads or stores Claude logins.

**Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**A new Settings.** One page per first-class harness (Overview, Models & providers, Instructions & memory, Extensions, Advanced), one Accounts & billing page, and one Other harnesses page for the basic tier. Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

**Basic-tier harnesses.** dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI and Goose can be used from the same app through the Agent Client Protocol. They are installed by you, show a Basic badge in the picker, and appear only after MoPilot Code has checked that the installed version works (Settings → Harnesses → Other harnesses shows the result and the reason when it doesn't). What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

**Computer use and browser control, for every harness.** Codex uses its own Browser and Computer use, and Claude Code on a claude.ai subscription uses Claude in Chrome, wherever those are installed on your Mac (you never need to open the ChatGPT or Claude apps). Everywhere else, and for every basic harness, MoPilot Code supplies its own tools, approval card, activity bar and stop button, so they work the same whichever model is running; a model that can't read images gets the screen described by a vision model, and the activity bar tells you where those screenshots go. You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. Settings → Built-in tools has Computer use, Browser and Voice & dictation.

**Your Chrome.** Browser control can use the Chrome you already have, with your signed-in sites, through the Playwright browser extension. You choose in Settings → Browser between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome; the choice applies to the whole app, each chat works in its own Chrome tab group, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code. The in-app browser and Your Chrome keep separate site permissions: sites you allowed before stay allowed in the in-app browser, Your Chrome asks the first time, and each permission card says which browser it is about.

**Accounts & billing in one place.** Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits live on one page, are selectable per chat, and a chat can switch account without losing its place. Your existing billing method does not change when you upgrade. Claude Code runs as your own `claude` CLI with the login you made there; MoPilot Code never reads or stores Claude logins.

**Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**Basic-tier harnesses.** dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI and Goose can be used from the same app through the Agent Client Protocol. They are installed by you, show a Basic badge in the picker, and appear only after MoPilot Code has checked that the installed version works (Settings → Harnesses → Other harnesses shows the result and the reason when it doesn't). What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

**Computer use and browser control, for every harness.** Codex uses its own Browser and Computer use, and Claude Code on a claude.ai subscription uses Claude in Chrome, wherever those are installed on your Mac (you never need to open the ChatGPT or Claude apps). Everywhere else, and for every basic harness, MoPilot Code supplies its own tools, approval card, activity bar and stop button, so they work the same whichever model is running; a model that can't read images gets the screen described by a vision model, and the activity bar tells you where those screenshots go. You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. Settings → Built-in tools has Computer use, Browser and Voice & dictation.

**Your Chrome.** Browser control can use the Chrome you already have, with your signed-in sites, through the Playwright browser extension. You choose in Settings → Browser between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome; the choice applies to the whole app, each chat works in its own Chrome tab group, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code. The in-app browser and Your Chrome keep separate site permissions: sites you allowed before stay allowed in the in-app browser, Your Chrome asks the first time, and each permission card says which browser it is about.

**Accounts & billing in one place.** Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits live on one page, are selectable per chat, and a chat can switch account without losing its place. Your existing billing method does not change when you upgrade. Claude Code runs as your own `claude` CLI with the login you made there; MoPilot Code never reads or stores Claude logins.

**Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**A new Settings.** One page per first-class harness (Overview, Models & providers, Instructions & memory, Extensions, Advanced), one Accounts & billing page, and one Other harnesses page for the basic tier. Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

They are installed by you, show a Basic badge in the picker, and appear only after MoPilot Code has checked that the installed version works (Settings → Harnesses → Other harnesses shows the result and the reason when it doesn't). What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

**Computer use and browser control, for every harness.** Codex uses its own Browser and Computer use, and Claude Code on a claude.ai subscription uses Claude in Chrome, wherever those are installed on your Mac (you never need to open the ChatGPT or Claude apps). Everywhere else, and for every basic harness, MoPilot Code supplies its own tools, approval card, activity bar and stop button, so they work the same whichever model is running; a model that can't read images gets the screen described by a vision model, and the activity bar tells you where those screenshots go. You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. Settings → Built-in tools has Computer use, Browser and Voice & dictation.

**Your Chrome.** Browser control can use the Chrome you already have, with your signed-in sites, through the Playwright browser extension. You choose in Settings → Browser between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome; the choice applies to the whole app, each chat works in its own Chrome tab group, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code. The in-app browser and Your Chrome keep separate site permissions: sites you allowed before stay allowed in the in-app browser, Your Chrome asks the first time, and each permission card says which browser it is about.

**Accounts & billing in one place.** Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits live on one page, are selectable per chat, and a chat can switch account without losing its place. Your existing billing method does not change when you upgrade. Claude Code runs as your own `claude` CLI with the login you made there; MoPilot Code never reads or stores Claude logins.

**Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**A new Settings.** One page per first-class harness (Overview, Models & providers, Instructions & memory, Extensions, Advanced), one Accounts & billing page, and one Other harnesses page for the basic tier. Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

Everywhere else, and for every basic harness, MoPilot Code supplies its own tools, approval card, activity bar and stop button, so they work the same whichever model is running; a model that can't read images gets the screen described by a vision model, and the activity bar tells you where those screenshots go. You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. Settings → Built-in tools has Computer use, Browser and Voice & dictation.

**Your Chrome.** Browser control can use the Chrome you already have, with your signed-in sites, through the Playwright browser extension. You choose in Settings → Browser between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome; the choice applies to the whole app, each chat works in its own Chrome tab group, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code. The in-app browser and Your Chrome keep separate site permissions: sites you allowed before stay allowed in the in-app browser, Your Chrome asks the first time, and each permission card says which browser it is about.

**Accounts & billing in one place.** Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits live on one page, are selectable per chat, and a chat can switch account without losing its place. Your existing billing method does not change when you upgrade. Claude Code runs as your own `claude` CLI with the login you made there; MoPilot Code never reads or stores Claude logins.

**Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**A new Settings.** One page per first-class harness (Overview, Models & providers, Instructions & memory, Extensions, Advanced), one Accounts & billing page, and one Other harnesses page for the basic tier. Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

You choose in Settings → Browser between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome; the choice applies to the whole app, each chat works in its own Chrome tab group, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code. The in-app browser and Your Chrome keep separate site permissions: sites you allowed before stay allowed in the in-app browser, Your Chrome asks the first time, and each permission card says which browser it is about.

**Accounts & billing in one place.** Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits live on one page, are selectable per chat, and a chat can switch account without losing its place. Your existing billing method does not change when you upgrade. Claude Code runs as your own `claude` CLI with the login you made there; MoPilot Code never reads or stores Claude logins.

**Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**A new Settings.** One page per first-class harness (Overview, Models & providers, Instructions & memory, Extensions, Advanced), one Accounts & billing page, and one Other harnesses page for the basic tier. Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. **Accounts & billing in one place.** Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits live on one page, are selectable per chat, and a chat can switch account without losing its place. Your existing billing method does not change when you upgrade. Claude Code runs as your own `claude` CLI with the login you made there; MoPilot Code never reads or stores Claude logins.

**Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**A new Settings.** One page per first-class harness (Overview, Models & providers, Instructions & memory, Extensions, Advanced), one Accounts & billing page, and one Other harnesses page for the basic tier. Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. **Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**A new Settings.** One page per first-class harness (Overview, Models & providers, Instructions & memory, Extensions, Advanced), one Accounts & billing page, and one Other harnesses page for the basic tier. Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

**You don't need Codex to use MoPilot Code.** Files, the terminal, `@` file mentions, ⌘K search, projects, worktrees, scheduled tasks and notifications are MoPilot Code's own. With only Claude Code installed, everything works.

**Basic-tier harnesses.** dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI and Goose can be used from the same app through the Agent Client Protocol. They are installed by you, show a Basic badge in the picker, and appear only after MoPilot Code has checked that the installed version works (Settings → Harnesses → Other harnesses shows the result and the reason when it doesn't). What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

**Computer use and browser control, for every harness.** Codex uses its own Browser and Computer use, and Claude Code on a claude.ai subscription uses Claude in Chrome, wherever those are installed on your Mac (you never need to open the ChatGPT or Claude apps). Everywhere else, and for every basic harness, MoPilot Code supplies its own tools, approval card, activity bar and stop button, so they work the same whichever model is running; a model that can't read images gets the screen described by a vision model, and the activity bar tells you where those screenshots go. You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. Settings → Built-in tools has Computer use, Browser and Voice & dictation.

**Your Chrome.** Browser control can use the Chrome you already have, with your signed-in sites, through the Playwright browser extension. You choose in Settings → Browser between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome; the choice applies to the whole app, each chat works in its own Chrome tab group, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code. The in-app browser and Your Chrome keep separate site permissions: sites you allowed before stay allowed in the in-app browser, Your Chrome asks the first time, and each permission card says which browser it is about.

On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

**A new Settings.** One page per first-class harness (Overview, Models & providers, Instructions & memory, Extensions, Advanced), one Accounts & billing page, and one Other harnesses page for the basic tier. Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.

They are installed by you, show a Basic badge in the picker, and appear only after MoPilot Code has checked that the installed version works (Settings → Harnesses → Other harnesses shows the result and the reason when it doesn't). What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

**Computer use and browser control, for every harness.** Codex uses its own Browser and Computer use, and Claude Code on a claude.ai subscription uses Claude in Chrome, wherever those are installed on your Mac (you never need to open the ChatGPT or Claude apps). Everywhere else, and for every basic harness, MoPilot Code supplies its own tools, approval card, activity bar and stop button, so they work the same whichever model is running; a model that can't read images gets the screen described by a vision model, and the activity bar tells you where those screenshots go. You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. Settings → Built-in tools has Computer use, Browser and Voice & dictation.

You choose in Settings → Browser between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome; the choice applies to the whole app, each chat works in its own Chrome tab group, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code. The in-app browser and Your Chrome keep separate site permissions: sites you allowed before stay allowed in the in-app browser, Your Chrome asks the first time, and each permission card says which browser it is about.

Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

**Codex and Claude Code, side by side.** Both are first-class. Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). They are installed by you, show a Basic badge in the picker, and appear only after MoPilot Code has checked that the installed version works (Settings → Harnesses → Other harnesses shows the result and the reason when it doesn't). What basic harnesses get, and don't get, is under "Known limits".

**Computer use and browser control, for every harness.** The same tools, approval card, activity bar and stop button work with Codex, Claude Code and every basic harness. MoPilot Code supplies them, so they work the same whichever model is running; a model that can't read images gets the screen described by a vision model, and the activity bar tells you where those screenshots go. You can take over by moving the mouse, and Esc stops the agent. Apps you haven't allowed are never controlled, and the agent never controls MoPilot Code itself, System Settings or Keychain Access. Settings → Built-in tools has Computer use, Browser and Voice & dictation.

**Your Chrome.** Browser control can use the Chrome you already have, with your signed-in sites, through the Playwright browser extension. You choose per chat between the MoPilot Code browser (a clean profile with none of your logins) and Your Chrome, and site permissions are managed in MoPilot Code.

**Accounts & billing in one place.** Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits live on one page, are selectable per chat, and a chat can switch account without losing its place. Your existing billing method does not change when you upgrade. Claude Code runs as your own `claude` CLI with the login you made there; MoPilot Code never reads or stores Claude logins.

**Goals and plan mode on both harnesses.** Codex goals work as before. Claude Code goals now have the same goal bar: they run inside a single turn, can be paused, resumed and cleared, and show their progress. A paused Claude Code goal keeps its condition, so you can resume it later. On metered billing (an API key or MoPilot credits) goals have a default limit so an unattended goal can't run up a bill: about 2M tokens for Codex (a soft limit) and 30 rounds for Claude Code, both marked "Limit set by MoPilot Code" and changeable. Subscriptions have no default limit. Plan mode works on both.

Codex's plugins, MCP, skills and hooks, and Claude Code's MCP servers, plugins and hooks, sit on their own pages.

**Scheduled tasks.** Run a task with Codex or Claude Code on this Mac. Computer control is off by default for a task, and you choose what happens when approval is needed: wait and notify, or skip that run.

**Quit and update safety.** Quitting or restarting to update tells you what will stop (running turns, background workflows, active goals). Goals are paused, not lost.

Each chat runs on the harness that created it, and both get the same chat experience: goals, plan mode, code review, compact, init, skills, background tasks, rename, fork, archive and search (workflows exist only in Claude Code; where a harness has no `init` or `!` shell of its own, MoPilot Code supplies it). Codex's own commands and Claude Code's own slash commands, skills and workflows appear in the `/` menu and are passed through as you type them. Where one harness has no equivalent, the entry says why and, when the other harness can do it, offers to use that one (for example, voice chat and Codex Cloud are Codex features, and Claude Code chats offer to start a Codex chat for them). The full list of what each harness does is in `docs/harness-matrix.md`, and Settings → Harnesses → Compatibility shows the same table.
